steps.observation: You have 10 seconds. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
DNA vs. RNA—key contrasts:

• Sugar: DNA has deoxyribose (lacks one oxygen), RNA has ribose.  
• Bases: DNA uses A-T-C-G; RNA swaps thymine (T) for uracil (U).  
• Strands: DNA is mostly double-stranded; RNA is usually single-stranded.  
• Stability: DNA is chemically sturdier, suited for long-term info storage; RNA is shorter-lived and more reactive.  
• Roles: DNA stores the genome; RNA acts as messenger (mRNA), translator (tRNA, rRNA), and regulator (siRNA, miRNA, etc.).  
• Location: DNA stays mainly in the nucleus (and mitochondria/chloroplasts); RNA is synthesized in the nucleus but functions largely in the cytoplasm.
